sl.wood-plane.where: slider: how far the saw plane stands from the log's axis. Low is quartersawn, high is plainsawn - this one control is the whole range of cuts

sl.wood-y0.where: slider: where along the saw plane the board is taken from

sl.wood-wid.where: slider: how wide the plank is, in the same units as the trunk radius. It may be set WIDER than the log, which is how a live-edge slab is cut

sl.wood-len.where: slider: how far along the trunk the plank runs. With the width it sets the board's proportions, so it also decides whether a round knot renders round

sl.wood-cutAngle.where: slider: which way round the trunk the saw plane faces, in degrees. 0 to 179, because 180 is the same plane cut from the other side

sl.wood-treeDia.where: slider: the log's diameter in feet. A readout you can drag — it shows the size the rings actually came to, and dragging solves once for the ring-width scale rather than pinning the size

lbl.kept-cuts.where: label: the group of saved board cuts the floor is laid from

a11y.wood-set.where: accessible name for the kept-cuts button group

tool.keep-cut.where: button: save the board currently shown, so the floor is laid from it and any others kept

tool.clear-cuts.where: button: discard every kept cut and go back to cutting one log

placeholders.n: how many cuts are now kept, e.g. 3

hint.cut-kept.where: status shown after keeping a cut

hint.cuts-cleared.where: status after discarding every kept cut

hint.cuts-full.where: status when trying to keep a ninth cut

sl.wood-plankLen.where: slider: nominal plank length in inches, capped at the board's own length

sl.wood-plankVary.where: slider: how much plank lengths differ from the nominal, 0 = all identical

sl.wood-plankStagger.where: slider: how far each row's end joints shift from the row below, 0 = joints stack into columns

tile.pat.plank.where: button: the plank-run floor layout, rows of varying-length boards with staggered end joints

sl.wood-trunkH.where: slider: the whole tree's height from stump to apex, in feet

sl.wood-taper.where: slider: how hard the leader's yearly height increment tracks that year's ring width. 0 means it was always at full height, so the trunk is a cylinder

sl.wood-zBase.where: slider: how far up the trunk this board was cut, in feet above the stump

ui.wood-taper-note.where: explains that a trunk narrows because higher wood has FEWER rings, not thinner ones

sl.wood-stage.where: slider: how many different boards of the one log the floor is cut from. 1 repeats a single board; higher walks down the cant

sl.wood-rings.where: slider: how many growth rings the log has

sl.wood-late.where: slider: how dark the latewood band is - the contrast of the grain

sl.wood-lean.where: slider: how far the pith leans along the saw plane

sl.wood-leanFine.where: slider: a faster ripple on top of the pith's lean

sl.wood-wander.where: slider: how far the pith wanders across the board

sl.wood-wanderFine.where: slider: a faster ripple on top of the pith's wander

sl.wood-drift.where: slider: how far the colour wanders between the pith and the bark

sl.wood-driftRings.where: slider: how many rings the colour takes to wander that far - the correlation length, not a count of anything

sl.wood-sapRings.where: slider: how many rings inward from the bark are still sapwood - a count of rings, not a distance

sl.wood-sapFade.where: slider: how many rings the conversion from sapwood to heartwood takes - how abrupt the boundary looks

sl.wood-devAmp.where: slider: how far the growth rings bulge away from being circles

sl.wood-devAngle.where: slider: which way round the trunk the bulge points, in degrees

sl.wood-devSpread.where: slider: how much of the trunk's circumference the bulge covers - narrow is a lump, wide is a lean

sl.wood-devStart.where: slider: the ring at which the bulge begins to form. Everything inside it stays round

sl.wood-devRamp.where: slider: how many rings the bulge takes to come fully on

sl.wood-dev2Amp.where: slider: how far the trunk swells where a branch leaves it

sl.wood-dev2Angle.where: slider: which way round the trunk the branch points, in degrees

sl.wood-dev2Spread.where: slider: how much of the trunk's circumference the branch disturbs

sl.wood-dev2Z.where: slider: where ALONG the trunk the branch sits - the control that makes it a branch and not a lean

sl.wood-dev2ZSpan.where: slider: how far along the trunk the branch's influence reaches either side

sl.wood-dev2Start.where: slider: the ring at which the branch begins. Wood inside it is untouched

sl.wood-dev2Ramp.where: slider: how many rings the branch takes to come fully on

sl.wood-dev2Knot.where: slider: how fast the branch cone widens, which sets how big the knot face is. 0 draws no face

sl.wood-dev2KnotPitch.where: slider: how tight the branch's own growth rings are inside the knot face

sl.wood-dev2Die.where: slider: the ring at which the branch died. 0 means it is still alive, so the knot runs to the bark; any other value stops it there and the trunk grows over it

sl.wood-waveAmp.where: slider: part of the shared wave family that makes a tree a species

sl.wood-waveK.where: slider: part of the shared wave family that makes a tree a species

sl.wood-waveZ.where: slider: part of the shared wave family that makes a tree a species

sl.wood-anchorAt.where: slider: part of the shared wave family that makes a tree a species

sl.wood-anchorOver.where: slider: part of the shared wave family that makes a tree a species

sl.wood-anchorTo.where: slider: part of the shared wave family that makes a tree a species

sl.wood-juv.where: slider: part of the growth curve - how a species puts on width over its life

sl.wood-decay.where: slider: part of the growth curve - how a species puts on width over its life

sl.wood-floor.where: slider: part of the growth curve - how a species puts on width over its life

sl.wood-vary.where: slider: part of the growth curve - how a species puts on width over its life

sl.wood-dRate.where: slider: part of the growth curve - how a species puts on width over its life

sl.wood-dDepth.where: slider: part of the growth curve - how a species puts on width over its life

sl.wood-lateFrac.where: slider: what fraction of each ring is the dark latewood band

sl.wood-lateSharp.where: slider: how abruptly the latewood begins - sharp in a fir, soft in a maple

sl.wood-gloss.where: slider: how strongly fibre direction shows as light and dark at all. 0 draws no figure

sl.wood-fibreSpiral.where: slider: a steady helical wind of the fibres about the trunk, in degrees

sl.wood-interlock.where: slider: how far the spiral angle swings when it alternates - interlocked grain, which is what gives ribbon figure

sl.wood-interlockRings.where: slider: how many years the spiral takes to reverse and come back

sl.wood-curl.where: slider: how far the fibres undulate across the trunk - fiddleback and quilt

sl.wood-curlRate.where: slider: how tightly that undulation repeats along the trunk

sl.wood-eyes.where: slider: how strongly the bird's-eye dimples show. 0 draws none

sl.wood-eyeSpacing.where: slider: how far apart the dimples sit on the cambium

sl.wood-eyeSize.where: slider: how wide each eye is, in inches

sl.wood-eyeDepth.where: slider: how far the growth rings dip into a dimple - the dip is what makes the little concentric circles
